title: ATS-Friendly Resume Format India: Layout, Order, Sample
description: A practical ATS-friendly resume format for India: single-column layout, section order for freshers, education lines and a line-by-line sample.
h1: ATS-friendly resume format in India: layout, section order and a sample
keywords: ats friendly resume format for freshers

sections.title: The layout to keep and the elements to drop
sections.content:
Use one column, with ordinary text from top to bottom. Leave margins of roughly 1.5 to 2 cm, choose a standard font such as Calibri, Arial or Cambria at 10 to 12 points, and use plain round bullets. Write dates in one pattern throughout, for example 'Jun 2025 - Aug 2025'.

Drop tables, text boxes, icons, skill bars, charts and background graphics. They add little information and are exactly the elements that parsing guides, including Greenhouse's, associate with extraction problems.

sections.title: Section order for a fresher
sections.content:
A common order is: name and contact line, a two or three line summary (optional), education, skills, projects, internships, certifications, and achievements. Because a fresher has little employment history, education usually comes first.

The order is a judgement call, not a rule. If your strongest evidence is a well-built project or a relevant internship, move that section above education. Within each section, list the newest item first.

sections.title: A sample layout, line by line
sections.content:
Here is an illustrative outline you can adapt. Header: 'Aarav Sharma', then 'Jaipur, Rajasthan | +91 98XXXXXX10 | aarav.example@gmail.com | linkedin.com/in/aaravsharma | github.com/aaravsharma'.

Then: 'Summary' (two lines on your degree, target role and strongest skill area); 'Education' (B.Tech, Computer Science and Engineering, institute name, university, 2021-2025, CGPA 8.2/10); 'Skills' (Languages: Python, Java, SQL; Web: HTML, CSS, Django; Tools: Git, VS Code); 'Projects' (two or three, each with two bullets); 'Internships'; 'Certifications'. All details here are illustrative.

sections.title: Writing the education lines
sections.content:
Give the degree, branch, institute, university or board, and the years. State your score the way your marksheet does and add the scale: 'CGPA 8.2/10' or '78.4%'. If you mix formats between sections, a recruiter has to convert them in their head.

Include Class XII and Class X only where the application asks for them or where your target employers commonly check them. If you took a gap, show the real dates rather than stretching them. Honest and consistent beats tidy and wrong.

sections.title: The contact line and links
sections.content:
Put your name and contact details in the main body of the page, not inside the document header, because some parsers skip header and footer areas. Use +91 before your number, a professional email address and your city and state.

Add LinkedIn and GitHub only if the profiles are current and relevant, and write them out as visible text so they survive conversion to plain text.

sections.title: Adjusting the format by role and experience
sections.content:
For software roles, group skills into languages, frameworks, databases and tools. For commerce, operations or sales roles, list the systems and methods you have used, such as Tally, Excel or CRM tools, and put internships or project work ahead of generic skill lists.

A fresher resume normally fits on one page. If you have three or more years of experience and the second page carries real, relevant content, two pages are acceptable.

faqs.q: Should I use a two-column template if it looks better?
faqs.a: For online applications, a single column is the more conservative choice because the reading order is unambiguous. If you love a designed version, keep it for networking or printing and submit a plain version through portals.

faqs.q: Should education or skills come first for a fresher?
faqs.a: Education usually leads because it is your main credential. Switch the order if your skills and projects are clearly stronger than your academic record, or if the job posting stresses a particular skill set.

faqs.q: How do I write my CGPA?
faqs.a: Copy it as your university reports it and add the scale, such as 8.2/10. If your institute uses a different scale, say so. Avoid converting to a percentage unless your university publishes an official conversion.

faqs.q: Can I add LinkedIn and GitHub links?
faqs.a: Yes, if the profiles are complete and relevant to the role. Spell the addresses out as text, and check that the repositories you want noticed have readable README files.

sections.content: Cognizant offers technology, digital and operations-related roles, and its fresher hiring steps vary by role, degree and cycle. This guide cannot confirm them. sections.title: A layout that reads quickly
sections.content:
Put your name and contact line at the top, then education, skills, projects, internships, certifications and achievements. Use a single column, standard headings and a plain font. One page is enough for most freshers.

If you already have a resume made in a builder such as NextCV, copy the text into a plain-text editor and check the order, because builders can sometimes reorder content when exporting.

sections.title: Group skills by how recruiters search
sections.content:
Cognizant postings, like most, name specific technologies. Group your skills in the same way: languages, databases, web or cloud tools, testing tools, and development practices such as Git or Agile basics. Include only those that appear in your projects, internships or coursework.

If a posting stresses testing or support rather than development, move relevant experience, such as manual test cases or helpdesk work, higher.

sections.title: Project lines for three kinds of graduate
sections.content: Software or IT degree: 'Developed a student feedback system with Python Flask and SQLite; created the form, storage and summary views.' Electronics or electrical: 'Built a soil-moisture monitor with a microcontroller and displayed readings on an LCD.' Commerce or science graduate applying to a process role: 'Reconciled 200 sample invoices in Excel during an internship and flagged mismatches for review.' sections.title: Teamwork and ownership
sections.content: Many fresher roles involve working inside teams on shared deliverables. A line that shows your own contribution within a group project is more useful than a claim to be a 'team player': 'Handled database design and testing in a team of four.' If you contributed to a repository, mention the repository.

sections.title: Final checks before applying
sections.content: Compare your degree name, year, CGPA and any arrears or gap details with your documents. Delete any unfilled template text. Confirm the file opens correctly, the links work and the name matches your application. Tailor the first two lines to the role you are applying to.

faqs.q: Which skills should I list for Cognizant roles?
faqs.a: Those stated in the specific vacancy that you can honestly demonstrate. Back the important ones with a project, internship, assignment or certification.

faqs.q: Should a mechanical or civil graduate use an IT resume format?
faqs.a: Use the layout, but lead with the evidence relevant to the role, such as CAD, analysis tools or an internship in your field. Apply to roles that your qualification is listed for.

faqs.q: Is an internship necessary?
faqs.a: No. If you have none, strengthen the projects section with clear contribution lines and add relevant courses or training.

title: Fresher Resume Format in India: Structure and Sample

sections.title: The structure most fresher resumes follow
sections.content:
A common structure runs: name and contact line, a short summary (optional), education, skills, projects, internships or training, certifications, and achievements or activities. It works because a fresher's main credentials are academic and practical, not employment history.

The order can change. If your best evidence is an internship, lead with it. If your academic record is your best asset, keep education first.

sections.title: Sample outline with example wording
sections.content:
Header: name, city and state, +91 phone number, email, and one profile link if relevant. Summary: 'B.Com graduate with Tally and Excel coursework, seeking an accounts executive role.' Education: degree, institute, university, years, score with scale. Skills: Tally Prime, MS Excel, basic GST entries. Experience: a three-month internship with specific tasks. The details above are illustrative.

The exact content will change with your degree and target role.

sections.title: How to write scores and dates
sections.content: State your CGPA with its scale ('7.9/10') or your percentage ('76.2%'), as your marksheet reports it. Write graduation years as ranges ('2022-2025') and keep the same style in every section. If you are awaiting final results, write 'Expected 2026' for the year rather than a result you do not yet have.

sections.title: One page, and what makes it fit
sections.content: Most freshers can fit the essentials on one page by using brief bullets, removing weak sections and avoiding large margins or spacing. Cut hobbies that do not relate to the role, school-level detail beyond Class X and XII scores and repeated skills. Aim for readability, not a smaller font.

sections.title: Personal details: what to include
sections.content: Include name, phone, email, city and state, and a LinkedIn or portfolio link if relevant. Items such as father's name, marital status or religion are not needed for most private-sector applications unless a form asks. Government and some institutional forms ask for specific personal details, and you should provide those on the form itself.

sections.title: How this differs from other fresher guides
sections.content: This page covers the standard structure. For building a resume from scratch, with prompts for gathering your material, see the fresher resume format guide. For choosing between format types, see the guide to the best fresher resume format. For ATS-specific layout rules, use the ATS-friendly format page.

faqs.q: Should I write 'Expected 2026' for my graduation year?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have not yet graduated. Add your latest semester score or CGPA so far, and update the resume when you receive your final result.

faqs.q: Do I need a career objective on a fresher resume?
faqs.a: It is optional. A short summary naming your degree, skills and target role can help. A generic sentence about 'seeking growth' adds nothing, so omit it.

faqs.q: How should I list school marks?
faqs.a: Include Class X and XII scores only if the application asks or the field commonly expects them. If you list them, use the same format as your marksheet.

faqs.q: Can a fresher resume have two pages?
faqs.a: Rarely needed. Consider it only if you have substantial, relevant material such as several internships or published work.

Date style should be uniform, such as 'Jul 2024 - Dec 2024'.

sections.title: Skills and certifications for a global audience
sections.content: List skills in the terms used in international job postings, for example 'Microsoft Excel', 'Java' or 'SQL'. title: Resume vs CV in India: Key Differences Explained
description: See how a resume and a CV differ in length, content and purpose, and how the two terms are actually used by Indian employers and institutions.
h1: Resume vs CV in India: the key differences

sections.title: How the terms are used in India
sections.content: In everyday Indian hiring, 'CV' and 'resume' are often used for the same document, and many recruiters ask for a 'CV' when they mean a two-page career summary. The distinction is clearer in academic and international contexts. Knowing both meanings helps you send the right document.

sections.title: What a resume is
sections.content: A resume is a short, targeted summary of your education, skills and experience, usually one or two pages. It is tailored to a specific role and leaves out anything that does not support the application. It is the standard document for private-sector jobs and internships.

sections.title: What a CV is
sections.content: A curriculum vitae is a fuller record of your academic and professional history. It can run to several pages and include publications, research, teaching experience, conferences, grants and awards. It is typical for academic, research, scientific and some medical or international applications.

sections.title: Side-by-side differences
sections.content: Length: resume one to two pages; CV as long as the record needs. Purpose: resume is tailored to a job; CV records the full history. Content: resume selects the most relevant items; CV lists them all. Update pattern: a resume is rewritten per role; a CV grows over time and is trimmed less. Typical use: resume for corporate roles; CV for research, teaching and fellowships.

sections.title: Which one do freshers need
sections.content: Most freshers applying to companies need a one-page resume, even when the posting says 'CV'. A fresher applying for a research internship, an MS or PhD programme, or a teaching assistant post may need a CV with academic details. If in doubt, follow the posting's wording and length hints.

sections.title: Document readiness
sections.content: Whichever you send, keep the layout simple, dates consistent and contact details clear. For software reading, a single-column, text-based file is the safest. The companion guide on when to send which explains how to decide by situation.

faqs.q: Is a CV longer than a resume in India?
faqs.a: Often, yes, for academic and research uses. In corporate hiring the two terms are used loosely, and a one- or two-page document is typical for both.

faqs.q: Do I write 'CV' or 'Resume' at the top of the document?
faqs.a: Neither is needed. Put your name at the top instead and let the headings explain the content.

faqs.q: Do abroad employers use different terms?
faqs.a: Usage varies by country. In some places 'CV' means a short job document and in others a long academic record, so read the posting.

faqs.q: Can I convert my resume into a CV?
faqs.a: Yes, by adding the full history: publications, presentations, research and teaching details. Keep structure and dates consistent.

title: TCS Resume Format for Freshers: What to Include

h1: TCS resume format for freshers

sections.title: How fresher applications reach TCS
sections.content:
TCS runs the National Qualifier Test (NQT) as a route into fresher hiring, and its careers page for the test carries a note that the eligibility shown there is initial, generic guidance. Campus drives and individual job postings are other routes. Which one applies to you decides which forms you fill in and when a resume is requested.

No article can tell you the current dates, cut-offs or eligibility. Read the live TCS page for your batch and your degree before you prepare anything.

sections.title: Why consistency matters more than design here
sections.content:
Large fresher drives involve profile forms, test registrations and document checks. Your resume should repeat exactly what you entered elsewhere: degree and branch names, year of passing, CGPA or percentage and any answers about gaps or arrears. If a form asks and your resume says something different, you will have to explain the difference later.

So before you polish the layout, copy your details from your marksheets and use them everywhere.

sections.title: A sensible section order for an engineering fresher
sections.content:
Start with your name and contact line, then education, skills, projects, internships or training, certifications and achievements. A two-line summary is optional. If a project or internship is your strongest evidence for the role, move it above education.

Keep it to one page, in a single column, using ordinary headings. The structural advice in NextCV's ATS-friendly format guide applies here without change.

sections.title: Describing projects for a technical interview
sections.content:
Interviewers often start from a project you list and ask you to explain it, so write each entry as something you can talk through. State what the application did, which parts you built, and the tools. A CSE example: 'Built an inventory tracker in Java with MySQL; wrote the stock-update and report modules; handled input validation.' An ECE example: 'Interfaced a temperature sensor with an Arduino board and logged readings over serial; wrote the calibration routine.'

If you could not explain a line for five minutes, shorten it or remove it.

sections.title: Skills to list and how to word them
sections.content: Group skills by type: programming languages, databases, web or core-engineering tools, and basic computing subjects such as data structures. List the ones you have actually used in a project, an assignment or a coding platform. If a posting names a tool you only know a little, mention it inside the relevant project line rather than in a confident skills row.

sections.title: If you are from BCA, BSc or MCA
sections.content: Degree eligibility differs by drive and changes between cycles, so check the current TCS page for your qualification instead of relying on a forum post. In the resume itself, BCA and BSc applicants should lead with programming coursework and the final-year project, and MCA applicants with the advanced project or dissertation, since the degree title alone says less than the work behind it.

sections.title: Mistakes common in high-volume fresher drives
sections.content: Sending the same resume to twenty companies without reading any of the postings is the main one. Others are naming the wrong company in a summary line, listing every language you have touched, leaving out your CGPA scale, and letting a certificate from an unrelated course take up space that a project should have. Re-read the file once as if you were the interviewer.

faqs.q: Does TCS require a particular resume format?
faqs.a: NextCV cannot confirm that TCS requires a specific resume template, so do not assume one. Requirements can vary by drive, so follow whatever the portal, your placement cell or the recruiter's email specifies.

faqs.q: Should I mention my NQT result on the resume?
faqs.a: Only if you have a result you can state accurately and it is relevant, for example under achievements with the test name and year. Do not describe scores or ranks you cannot show if asked.

faqs.q: Can I reuse my TCS resume for other companies?
faqs.a: Yes for the core content. Change the summary line, the order of skills and the lead project to suit each posting, and remove any reference to another company's name.

faqs.q: How much should I write about a final-year project?
faqs.a: Two or three lines are enough on the resume: purpose, your contribution and tools. Keep the rest for the interview, where you can explain design choices and what you would change.

sections.title: Writing project lines for the technical round
sections.content:
Pick two or three projects and describe each in two lines. For a web project: 'Built a college event portal in PHP and MySQL; implemented registration and admin approval.' For a data project: 'Cleaned a 10,000-row sales dataset in Python and built a monthly summary chart.' Use figures only if you really counted them.

Prepare to explain every tool named; interviewers can pick any of them.

sections.title: Skills: depth over length
sections.content: List core languages first, then web or database tools, then version control and development tools. Remove anything you could not answer a basic question about. A shorter skills list that matches your projects is more credible than a long list that does not.

sections.title: Non-engineering and diploma applicants
sections.content: If you hold a BCA, BSc or another degree, check which roles and drives accept your qualification. Where you are eligible, lead with the practical work that shows the skills in the posting: programming assignments, a final-year project or relevant training. Where the posting is for a non-technical role, emphasise communication, coordination and any tool experience instead.

sections.title: Keeping every form and your resume in agreement
sections.content: Infosys, like other large employers, may ask you to fill in your academic details on a form and later verify them against documents. Copy details from your marksheets and use the same spellings, scores and dates on every document. Disagreements are easy to avoid and hard to explain.

faqs.q: Does Infosys publish an official resume template for freshers?
faqs.a: NextCV cannot confirm that Infosys requires a specific fresher resume template, so do not assume one. Follow the instructions of your campus drive or the application page you are using.

faqs.q: Should I list HackWithInfy or InfyTQ on my resume?
faqs.a: Only if you took part or earned a result you can state accurately. Give the programme name, year and outcome. Registration alone is not something to present as an achievement.

faqs.q: Are coding profile links useful?
faqs.a: They help when the profile is active and shows real problem-solving. Write the address as text and keep only the one or two profiles you would be comfortable discussing.

faqs.q: How many pages should an Infosys fresher resume run to?
faqs.a: One page is the usual starting point for a fresher. Add a second page only when it holds relevant content that cannot be cut, such as extra internships or published work.

title: Wipro Resume Format for Freshers: Skills and Layout

sections.title: Start from the current Wipro posting
sections.content:
Wipro hires across technology, consulting and business-process work, and the eligibility and selection steps differ by role and by campaign. Read the specific vacancy or campus notice and note its role name, qualifications and the skills it lists.

sections.title: Show that you can learn a stack, not only that you know one
sections.content:
Many IT services employers train new joiners on technologies decided after hiring, so evidence of learning speed is often as useful as a long tool list. Show it through what you have done: a course completed on your own, a language picked up for a project, a certification with a project built from it.

One line such as 'Learned React over six weeks to build the front end of a student notes app' says more than the word 'quick learner'.

sections.title: Writing skill levels honestly
sections.content: Avoid star ratings. If you want to signal depth, do it by grouping: 'Used in projects: Java, SQL' and 'Familiar from coursework: C++, networking basics'. That separation tells the reader what you can do now and what you have only studied, and it prepares you for the questions you will get.

sections.title: Project examples for different backgrounds
sections.content:
Computer science: 'Built a library management system in Java and MySQL with issue, return and fine modules.' Electronics: 'Designed a basic home-automation prototype using a microcontroller and relay module; wrote the control code.' BCA or BSc: 'Created a responsive portfolio site in HTML, CSS and JavaScript; added a contact form with validation.'

All examples are illustrative. Replace them with your own work and the tools you used.

sections.title: Communication and teamwork evidence
sections.content: Client-facing and team-based work means written and spoken communication count. Show it with specifics: led a four-member project team, presented a project at a college symposium, wrote documentation for a final-year project. Leave out adjectives such as 'excellent communicator' unless something on the page proves it.

sections.title: Check before you submit
sections.content: Use a single column with standard headings and one page: contact line, summary if useful, education, skills, projects, internships, certifications, achievements, with an internship ahead of projects if it is your strongest material. Confirm that your degree, year, score and any gap details match your records, that the file opens as a text-based document, and that links work. Make sure the summary line does not name a different employer. Save the file with your name so the recruiter can find it.

faqs.q: Is there an official Wipro resume template?

faqs.q: What if I am from a non-technical degree?
faqs.a: Apply to roles listed for your qualification and show relevant tools, internships and communication evidence. Check the posting's eligibility rather than assuming an IT resume format fits.

faqs.q: Should I list every programming language I have seen?
faqs.a: No. List those you have used in a project or assignment, and separate them from topics you have only studied. Interviewers tend to ask about whatever is on the page.

faqs.q: Is a cover letter necessary for freshers?
faqs.a: Only when the application asks for one. A clear resume and accurate form answers carry most of the weight in fresher applications.

title: ATS-Friendly Resume Checklist: Final Checks Before You Apply
description: A pre-submission checklist for Indian job seekers covering file, layout, content, keyword match and consistency, so errors surface before you apply.
h1: ATS-friendly resume checklist: what to check before you submit

sections.title: File checks
sections.content: Confirm the file type matches what the portal asks for. Open the exported file, not the editing copy, and check that the text is selectable. Keep the size small; Greenhouse documents a 2.5 MB parsing limit, and other systems have their own. Name the file with your name and the word Resume, for example 'Aarav_Sharma_Resume.pdf'.

sections.title: Layout checks
sections.content: Check that the resume is a single column with no tables, text boxes, icons, charts or skill bars. Make sure your name and contact details are in the body of the page rather than the document header. Confirm headings are conventional and fonts are standard. Check that margins are even and the document is not crammed to reach one page.

sections.title: Content checks
sections.content: Check that each project or internship states what you did, with what tools, and the result. Confirm dates use one format and run in reverse order within each section. Make sure education lines show degree, institute, years and a score with its scale. Verify every phone number, email address and link by testing them.

sections.title: Job-match checks
sections.content: Compare the resume with the posting once more. Are the job title, key tools and required qualifications reflected where true? Are the most relevant items near the top? Remove any skill you could not discuss for two minutes in an interview, and check that no phrase has been copied directly from the posting.

sections.title: Consistency checks
sections.content: Compare the resume with your application form, LinkedIn and job-board profile. Degree names, graduation year, CGPA, skill names and dates should agree. If a form asks for details a resume normally leaves out, such as date of birth, enter them only there.

sections.title: The final read
sections.content: Run the plain-text test by pasting the content into a text editor, then read the pasted result slowly. Look for missing contact details, merged lines, odd characters and spelling errors. If possible, ask someone who has not seen the resume to tell you what role it seems to be aimed at.

faqs.q: How early should I run these checks before a deadline?
faqs.a: Do them at least a day before, if you can. Portals sometimes reject files or time out near closing time, and last-minute changes are when errors slip in.

faqs.q: Should I test the file on another device?
faqs.a: Yes. Opening it on a phone or a different computer shows whether fonts and spacing hold. It will not tell you how an employer's software parses it, but it catches layout problems.

faqs.q: What if the portal only accepts DOCX?
faqs.a: Provide a DOCX. Keep the formatting simple, and check the document for stray text boxes or tracked changes before exporting.

faqs.q: Does the file name matter?
faqs.a: It matters to the recruiter who downloads it. A clear name makes your file easy to find among many. Avoid spaces, special characters and names like 'final_final2'.

title: ATS-Friendly Resume Meaning: What It Does and Doesn't Cover
description: Understand what 'ATS-friendly' means for a resume, what it cannot promise, and how it differs from a resume that only looks polished.
h1: ATS-friendly resume meaning: what the term really covers
keywords: is an ats friendly resume necessary

sections.title: What 'ATS-friendly' means in plain words
sections.content:
An ATS-friendly resume is one whose text a piece of recruiting software can read correctly, and which a person can still skim quickly. That is the whole definition. It describes the file and the writing, not a certificate or a score you earn.

An applicant tracking system (ATS) is the database many employers use to collect applications, move candidates between hiring stages and search through them. When you upload a resume, many systems try to parse it: they pull your name, contact details, education, employers, dates and skills into separate fields. 'Friendly' simply means that extraction works.

sections.title: What the term does not mean
sections.content:
It does not mean guaranteed shortlisting, and it does not mean one special format that every employer's software prefers. Employers use different systems, and they configure them differently.

It also does not mean a machine rejects you for a missing keyword. Greenhouse's help documentation, for example, describes optional auto-reject rules that work on answers to application questions such as work authorisation or location, not on how a resume looks. The 'ATS score' you see on a free online checker is that tool's own estimate, not a number your employer sees.

sections.title: Readable by software versus readable by people
sections.content:
A resume can be attractive to a person and awkward for software. Skill bars and star ratings are a common case. A line such as 'Python ●●●●○' gives a parser the word Python and nothing useful about it, while a person has to guess what four dots mean. 'Python: used for a student attendance app and two coding-contest problems' works for both readers.

A plain, single-column resume tends to read the same way to a person and to a parser. That overlap is the practical core of ATS-friendly design.

sections.title: Two versions of the same fresher resume
sections.content:
Imagine one candidate with two files. In version A, the name and phone number sit inside a header text box, skills sit in a coloured sidebar, and small icons stand in for 'phone' and 'email'. In version B, the name and contact line are ordinary text at the top of the page, followed by headings: Education, Skills, Projects, Internships.

Greenhouse lists headers, text boxes, tables, columns and graphics among the things that can cause an unsuccessful parse. Version A risks arriving with the sidebar mixed into the education lines, or without a usable contact field. Version B is much less likely to have that problem.

sections.title: Why the idea matters in Indian hiring
sections.content:
Applications in India reach recruiters through several routes: company career portals, job boards, campus placement forms and plain email. Some recruitment platforms built for Indian employers, such as Naukri RMS from Info Edge, list resume parsing and resume search among their features.

You usually cannot tell which system a particular employer uses. So the sensible aim is a resume that survives parsing in general, rather than one tuned to a single tool you cannot see.

sections.title: A two-minute way to test the meaning yourself
sections.content:
Open your PDF, select all the text and paste it into Notepad or any plain-text editor. If nothing can be selected, the file is probably an image, which many parsers cannot read. If text appears, check that your name, phone number, headings and dates are in a sensible order and nothing has merged into a single line.

That quick test reveals more than a score on a website. To go further, read NextCV's guide on how to make a resume ATS-friendly, which walks through the full process.

faqs.q: Is an ATS-friendly resume the same as a plain, boring resume?
faqs.a: No. It means avoiding elements that break text extraction, such as tables, text boxes and image-only files. You can still use clear spacing, a restrained accent colour and bold headings, as long as the text stays selectable and in order.

faqs.q: Does a high score on an online ATS checker mean I will be shortlisted?
faqs.a: No. Each checker uses its own rules, and your employer's software may behave differently. Use a checker as a prompt to look for formatting problems, then decide for yourself whether the resume matches the job.

faqs.q: Do all Indian companies use an ATS?
faqs.a: There is no reliable way to say. Large employers commonly use recruitment software, while smaller firms may rely on email, spreadsheets or job-board inboxes. Writing a clean, parseable resume costs little, so it is worth doing either way.

faqs.q: Can an ATS-friendly resume still be rejected?
faqs.a: Yes. Recruiters decide on fit, eligibility, skills and the number of applicants. A readable file helps your details reach them accurately, but it cannot replace relevant skills or evidence.

title: ATS-Friendly Resume Tips for India: Small Fixes That Help
description: Practical ATS resume tips for Indian job seekers: wording, dates, links, fonts, photos and personal details, with short examples.
h1: ATS-friendly resume tips for Indian job seekers

sections.title: Use the same job titles and tool names the employer uses
sections.content: If a posting says 'Software Engineer', a resume that says 'Coder' or 'Programming Wizard' is harder to match. Write tool names the way the vacancy does, such as 'Microsoft Excel' or 'Power BI'. Where an abbreviation is common, write both once: 'Search Engine Optimisation (SEO)'.

sections.title: Keep dates, locations and labels uniform
sections.content: Pick one date style and use it everywhere: 'Jan 2025 - Apr 2025' throughout, not a mix of 'January 25', '1/25' and '2025'. Do the same for city and state, and for how you write degrees ('B.Tech' or 'B.E.', not both). Uniformity helps parsers recognise date ranges and helps recruiters scan.

sections.title: Write links as visible text
sections.content: A clickable 'GitHub' label can lose its address when text is extracted. Write 'github.com/yourname' and 'linkedin.com/in/yourname' in full. Check each link opens the right page before you submit.

sections.title: Keep the skills section specific
sections.content: Group skills the way a recruiter would search: 'Languages: Python, Java', 'Databases: MySQL, MongoDB', 'Tools: Git, Postman'. Skip ratings and bars. If you have only basic familiarity, say that in your projects or leave the skill out, because interviewers often ask about what you list.

sections.title: Be careful with fonts, symbols and bullets
sections.content: Stick with standard fonts and ordinary bullets. Unusual symbols, emoji and decorative characters may turn into question marks or odd characters in extracted text. Avoid using a symbol as the only separator in your contact line when a comma or vertical bar will do.

sections.title: Photos, date of birth and other Indian-resume add-ons
sections.content:
Many Indian templates carry a photo, date of birth, father's name or marital status. For most private-sector applications these are not needed unless the employer asks for them. A photo is an image element, and Greenhouse lists photos and graphics among possible parsing problems, so leaving it out is the more cautious choice.

If you are applying for roles where a form requests a date of birth or a photo, provide it in that form rather than on your resume. A 'Declaration' paragraph at the end rarely adds value and uses space you could spend on a project.

sections.title: Give the human reader a reason to continue
sections.content: Whatever the software does, a person reads the top of the page first. Lead with the line that best matches the job, whether that is a project, an internship or a certification. Add numbers where they are real, such as the number of users, records or test cases, and leave them out where they are guesses.

faqs.q: Should I put my photo on an ATS resume?
faqs.a: Unless the employer requests one, it is safer to leave it out. It adds no searchable information, and photos and graphics are named as a possible parsing issue by at least one major system's documentation.

faqs.q: Do I need to mention my date of birth?
faqs.a: Usually not. Provide it where an application form asks for it. Most resumes for private-sector jobs do well without it, and it takes up room you can use for skills or projects.

faqs.q: Is it fine to use abbreviations like ML, JS or HR?
faqs.a: Yes, but write the full term once, followed by the abbreviation in brackets. Recruiters may search for either version, and spelling both out once covers both.

faqs.q: How many keywords are too many?
faqs.a: There is no set number. If a term appears without a project, course or task behind it, it is probably padding. List the tools you can discuss in an interview and show at least some of them in action.

title: ATS Resume Best Practices for Freshers in India
description: How freshers can build ATS-readable resumes without job history: projects, internships, skills for the role and consistency across forms.
h1: ATS resume best practices for freshers
keywords: resume for campus placement vs off campus

sections.title: What freshers can offer without a job history
sections.content: Recruiters reading fresher resumes do not expect years of employment. They look for evidence that you can do the work: projects, internships, relevant coursework, certifications, competitions, open-source contributions or coding-platform profiles. Rank this evidence by how closely it matches the role and put the closest match first.

sections.title: Make projects your main evidence
sections.content:
A good project entry names the problem, your part in it, the tools and the result. For example: 'Built an attendance tracker for a 60-student class using Flask and SQLite; added a monthly report export.' The numbers here are illustrative; use only figures you can defend.

Choose two to four projects that suit the target role. A well-described small project usually reads better than a long list of unexplained ones, and a public repository with a clear README helps a reviewer confirm it.

sections.title: Match skills to the role family
sections.content:
A resume for a software or IT services role should group languages, frameworks, databases and tools. A resume for an analyst role should show Excel, SQL and reporting tools together with a piece of analysis. A resume for a commerce or operations role should show the systems you have used and any coursework or internship tasks that involved them.

The point is not to add more keywords but to put the right ones next to evidence.

sections.title: Campus drives versus off-campus applications
sections.content:
For campus placements, your placement cell often circulates a required format or collects details through a form. Follow that instruction first, because it overrides general advice. For off-campus roles, you will usually upload a file to a company portal or job board, so the formatting guidance on parsing matters more.

If you use Naukri or a similar board, keep the profile headline, key skills and dates consistent with your resume.

sections.title: Keep every version of your details consistent
sections.content: Your resume, application form, LinkedIn profile and any job-board profile should agree on degree names, graduation year, CGPA and skill labels. Small mismatches, such as 8.2 on one and 8.4 on another, can look careless or worse. Keep a master document and copy from it.

sections.title: What to leave out
sections.content: Leave out a long career objective, hobbies unrelated to the role, school-level achievements from many years back and skills you cannot discuss. Do not copy a job description into your skills list. A shorter resume with relevant evidence gives the reader less to wade through.

faqs.q: Should freshers put projects above education?
faqs.a: If your projects are the strongest match for the job, yes. If your degree, branch or score is the main credential, keep education first. Decide by what a recruiter should see in the first few lines.

faqs.q: How many projects should a fresher list?
faqs.a: Two to four is usually enough, provided each is described with your role and tools. Quality of description matters more than count.

faqs.q: Are certifications from NPTEL, Coursera or similar platforms worth listing?
faqs.a: List them when they relate to the job, and include the issuing platform and year. Unrelated certificates add length without adding evidence.

faqs.q: Should I mention a short or unpaid internship?
faqs.a: Yes, if the work is relevant. State the real duration and describe what you did. Do not inflate a short internship into a long-term role.

title: ATS Resume Optimization: Tailor Keywords to the Job
description: Learn how to tailor your resume to a job description honestly: extract keywords, place them with proof and know when not to add one.
h1: ATS resume optimization: tailoring a resume to a job description
keywords: how to add keywords to resume

sections.title: What optimisation realistically means
sections.content: Optimising a resume for an ATS does not mean tricking software. It means describing your real background in the vocabulary of a specific job, so that a recruiter who searches or skims for that vocabulary can find it. If you lack a skill, no phrasing changes that, and claiming it usually surfaces in the interview.

sections.title: Pull the keywords out of the job description
sections.content:
Read the posting and highlight three groups: must-have skills and tools, main responsibilities and qualifications. Take a junior data analyst vacancy as an example. The skills might be SQL, Excel and Power BI; the responsibilities might be building dashboards and reporting to a team; the qualification might be a degree in statistics, commerce or engineering.

Terms that appear more than once, or that the posting calls essential, deserve the most attention.

sections.title: Place keywords where they carry proof
sections.content: A keyword in the skills list shows that you know the name of a tool. The same keyword inside a bullet shows what you did with it. Before: 'Skills: SQL, Power BI.' After, in a project: 'Built a Power BI dashboard from a SQL sales table showing monthly revenue by region.' You can keep both: list the skill, then back it up.

sections.title: Handle synonyms and abbreviations
sections.content: Recruiters search with their own words. One may type 'machine learning', another 'ML'. Write the full term once with the abbreviation in brackets, and use whichever the posting uses for the rest. Do the same for degrees and tools, such as 'Bachelor of Commerce (B.Com)' or 'JavaScript (JS)'.

sections.title: When not to add a keyword
sections.content: Do not add a skill you cannot discuss. Do not paste the job description into the page, and do not hide keywords in white text. Hidden text can show up when the file is converted to plain text and looks like an attempt to mislead, which can hurt you more than a missing term would.

sections.title: How much to tailor each time
sections.content: Keep a strong base resume. For each role, adapt the summary, the order of your skills and your two or three most relevant bullets. If you find yourself rewriting the entire document each time, your base version may be too generic, or you may be applying to roles that are too different from each other.

faqs.q: Do I have to tailor my resume for every application?
faqs.a: It helps most when roles differ. For near-identical roles, a few edits to the summary and skills order may be enough. If the job has special requirements, deal with those first.

faqs.q: What is a 'match score' on resume tools?
faqs.a: It is that tool's own comparison of your text and a job description. It can point out missing terms, but it is not what an employer necessarily sees. Use it as a prompt, not a verdict.

faqs.q: Should I copy exact phrases from the job description?
faqs.a: Use the same names for skills and tools where they are true for you, but write your bullets in your own words. Copying whole sentences reads as generic and may not match what you did.

faqs.q: How many keywords should appear in my resume?
faqs.a: There is no target number. Include the terms that truthfully describe your experience and show them in context. If a keyword has no project or task behind it, consider removing it.

title: Best AI Resume Builder in India: How to Evaluate One
description: How to judge an AI resume builder in India: quality of writing suggestions, accuracy checks, ATS-readable exports and risks of invented details.
h1: Best AI resume builder in India: how to evaluate one

sections.title: Why this page does not name a winner
sections.content: Tools change often, and a ranking based on a quick look would be unreliable. Instead, this page shows how to test any AI resume builder yourself, using your real details, so that you pick one that fits your needs.

sections.title: What AI features can do
sections.content: AI features typically draft summaries, rewrite bullet points, suggest skills and tailor text to a job description. They can save time on phrasing. They cannot know what you actually did, so the quality depends on the facts you give and the checks you apply.

sections.title: The main risk: invented detail
sections.content: AI tools may add tools, figures or achievements you did not mention. Read every generated line. Delete anything you cannot explain. Compare: input 'made a quiz app'; risky output 'Developed a scalable quiz platform used by 5,000 students'; acceptable output 'Built a quiz app in Python with scoring and a question bank.'

sections.title: A test you can run
sections.content: Give the tool the same short set of facts: one project, one internship and a skills list. Check how it improves wording, whether it adds false specifics, whether it respects your facts and whether you can edit the output. Test it against a job description and see whether the suggestions are relevant, not copied.

sections.title: Export quality and ATS readability
sections.content: The finished file matters more than the AI. Export it, select the text and paste it into a plain-text editor. Check order, headings and dates. A beautiful template with scrambled text is a poor outcome. NextCV offers AI-assisted writing and resume-checking features; test them with the same procedure.

sections.title: Cost, data and fit
sections.content: Check the pricing model, including whether AI use is capped and whether payment recurs. Read how the tool uses your data. Choose the one whose writing you can verify, whose file passes your text test and whose terms are clear.

faqs.q: Can AI write my whole resume?
faqs.a: It can draft one, but you must supply the facts and verify each line. A resume with claims you cannot explain can hurt you in an interview.

faqs.q: Does using AI make my resume ATS-friendly?
faqs.a: Not automatically. Layout and file quality matter. Export and test the text order regardless of how the content was written.

faqs.q: Is an AI-written resume detectable?
faqs.a: Detection is unreliable, but generic phrasing is easy for readers to notice. Rewrite with specifics from your own work.

faqs.q: Should freshers use AI tools?
faqs.a: They can help with wording. Use them to improve clear facts you provide, and avoid accepting figures or tools you did not mention.

title: Best Resume Builder in India: Choosing by Your Needs
description: Choose a resume builder in India by what you need: template quality, export formats, editing access, pricing model and fit for freshers or experienced users.
h1: Best resume builder in India: choosing by your needs

sections.title: There is no single best builder
sections.content: The right builder depends on who you are and what you need. A student with one resume needs different features from a professional keeping several versions. This page gives criteria you can apply to any tool, rather than a list of ranked names that may be out of date.

sections.title: Criteria that matter
sections.content: Look at template quality, whether the exported text is readable, the formats you get, whether you can edit later, how many resume versions you can keep, whether it suits Indian conventions such as marks and scales and what the pricing model is. Rank these by your own needs.

sections.title: For freshers and students
sections.content: You probably need one clean one-page template, space for projects and education, easy editing and a low one-time cost. Skip tools that push many extras you will not use. Check that the education section handles CGPA and scale properly.

sections.title: For experienced professionals
sections.content: You may need multiple versions, two-page layouts, space for achievements and fast tailoring. Check whether the tool allows custom headings and reordering, and whether the export stays clean when the content grows.

sections.title: For non-IT and career changers
sections.content: Look for templates that do not assume a tech stack, with room for internships, tools and transferable skills. Check that you can rename sections and drop ones you do not need.

sections.title: A fair way to compare two builders
sections.content: Enter the same details in each. Export both. Select all text and paste into a plain-text editor. Compare readability, order and effort. Then compare the total cost and terms. NextCV lets users begin building and offers AI-assisted writing and resume-checking features, and its pricing page gives its current terms.

faqs.q: Which builder is best for freshers in India?
faqs.a: One that gives a clean one-page layout, handles education scores properly and has transparent pricing. Test with your own details before choosing.

faqs.q: Are more templates better?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. A few well-made, readable templates are better than many that export poorly.

faqs.q: Do I need to pay for a resume builder?
faqs.a: Not always. You can use a word processor for free. A builder is worth paying for if it saves time and produces a clean, readable file.

faqs.q: Can I move my resume between builders?

title: Best Resume Format for Freshers in India: Format Types

h1: Best resume format for freshers in India: choosing between formats

which resume format is best for freshers

sections.title: What 'best' depends on
sections.content: No format is best for everyone. The right one depends on your evidence, the role and how the application is processed. For most fresher applications in India, a simple, structured format works. This page compares the options so you can choose, rather than repeating a section-by-section template.

sections.title: Reverse-chronological format
sections.content: This lists the most recent item first within each section. It is the most widely understood format, and recruiters and software both expect it. It suits freshers with an internship or relevant projects. Its weakness is that, if your experience is thin or unrelated, the page may show little relevant evidence at the top.

sections.title: Functional (skills-based) format
sections.content: This groups content by skill rather than timeline. It can help someone with no direct experience, but it can hide dates and make a recruiter wonder what is missing. Some recruiters distrust it for that reason. For most freshers, a skills section inside a normal format does the job better.

sections.title: Combination format
sections.content: This begins with a skills or achievements summary, then follows with a chronological history of education, projects and internships. It suits freshers whose skills are clearly relevant, such as a coder with a strong project set. Keep the summary short or it will crowd out the rest.

sections.title: A quick way to choose
sections.content: If you have a relevant internship, use reverse-chronological with experience first. If you have strong projects but no internship, use reverse-chronological with projects above education. If you are changing fields, use the combination format with a short skills summary. If you are unsure, start with reverse-chronological.

sections.title: Format versus file and layout
sections.content: Format type is about content order. File and layout choices, such as single column and a text-based PDF, are separate and matter for software reading. Whatever type you choose, keep the layout simple and check the text-order test.

faqs.q: Which format is best for an IT fresher?
faqs.a: Reverse-chronological or combination, with skills and projects near the top. Keep it to one page and describe each project's tools and your contribution.

faqs.q: Is the functional format a bad idea?
faqs.a: It can work in rare cases, but it lacks dates and context, which many recruiters look for. Most freshers are better off with a standard format.

faqs.q: Does the best format change in 2026?
faqs.a: The fundamentals have not changed: clarity, relevance and parseable layout. Check the job posting for any specific document instructions.

faqs.q: Can I use two different formats for two applications?
faqs.a: Yes. Keep the same facts but change the order of sections to put the strongest evidence for each role first.

title: Best Resume Format for IT Jobs in India: Dev to QA

sections.title: What makes an IT resume different
sections.content: An IT resume is read for technology fit. The reviewer wants to see languages, tools and the kind of systems you have worked on quickly. That calls for a skills section that is organised, project and experience lines that name technologies, and links to code or products where possible.

sections.title: Grouping the technical skills
sections.content: Group skills by type: languages, frameworks and libraries, databases, cloud and DevOps tools, testing tools, and version control. Within each group, list the ones you can discuss. Avoid proficiency bars. If a skill is recent, show it in a project line rather than in a confident list.

sections.title: Writing development project lines
sections.content: State the system, your contribution and the stack. 'Built a REST API for a bookstore app using Node.js and MongoDB; implemented authentication and search endpoints.' Add what you tested or deployed. For team projects, name your part. A link to a repository with a clear README helps verify the claim.

sections.title: Experience and internship lines
sections.content: For internships and jobs, describe tasks and results: 'Fixed 12 front-end defects in a React dashboard and reduced page load time by caching API responses.' Use figures only if you know how they were measured. Mention tools, team size and the process you followed, such as Agile sprints.

sections.title: Adjusting for different IT roles
sections.content: Developers lead with projects and code. QA and testing candidates show test-case design, tools such as Selenium or Postman, and bug-reporting experience. Data candidates show SQL, Python or BI tools with a dataset-based project. Support and cloud roles show operating systems, ticketing tools, scripting and certifications.

sections.title: Education, certifications and length
sections.content: Keep education concise. Add certifications only if they relate to the role, with the provider and year. A fresher resume fits on one page; experienced IT professionals may use two, with recent work in detail and older roles in a line or two.

faqs.q: Should I include every programming language I know?
faqs.a: List the ones you have used in projects or work. A long list without evidence invites questions you may not be able to answer.

faqs.q: Is a GitHub link necessary?
faqs.a: Not necessary, but helpful if it shows real, readable projects. Remove it if the profile is empty.

faqs.q: How do I show cloud skills as a fresher?
faqs.a: Through a course with a hands-on project, such as deploying a small web app, and a clear description of the services you used.

faqs.q: What is a good way to describe a team project?
faqs.a: State the project, your role and the stack. For example: 'Developed the login and profile modules in a four-member team using Django.'

title: Career Objective for Resume for Freshers: Examples and Tips
description: How to write a career objective or summary for a fresher resume: when to use one, examples for different degrees and phrases to avoid.
h1: Career objective for a fresher resume
keywords: career objective for resume for freshers

sections.title: Objective or summary: which to use
sections.content: A career objective states what you want; a summary states what you offer. For freshers, a short combination of both works: your degree, your strongest skill area and the role you are targeting. If you cannot say anything specific, skip the section; a resume without an objective is fine.

sections.title: A simple formula
sections.content: Write two lines: who you are, what you can do, and the role you want. 'B.Tech Computer Science graduate with Java and SQL project experience, seeking a software engineer role.' Replace the degree, skills and role with your own. Tailor the last part for each application.

sections.title: Examples for different backgrounds
sections.content: BCA: 'BCA graduate with PHP and MySQL project experience, seeking a web developer role.' Commerce: 'B.Com graduate with Tally and Excel internship experience, seeking an accounts executive role.' Electronics: 'ECE graduate with embedded systems project experience, seeking a hardware or firmware trainee role.' Management: 'BBA graduate with market survey and Excel analysis experience, seeking an operations associate role.'

sections.title: Phrases to avoid
sections.content: Avoid 'seeking a challenging position in a reputed organisation to utilise my skills and grow'. It fits everyone, and so says nothing. Avoid claims such as 'highly motivated' unless the rest of the page shows it, and avoid naming one company if you reuse the resume.

sections.title: Where it sits and how long it should be
sections.content: Place it directly under your contact line, in two or three lines at most. If your resume has a skills-based layout, the summary can lead into your skills. Keep it plain and readable so that recruiters see it quickly.

sections.title: Check your objective against the posting
sections.content: Compare your summary to the job posting. Does it name the same role, and does the skill mentioned match what the vacancy asks for? If not, adjust it. A summary that points in a different direction from the posting can make the match look weaker.

faqs.q: Is a career objective mandatory for freshers?
faqs.a: No. Use one only if it adds specific information about your skills and target role.

faqs.q: How long should a career objective be?
faqs.a: Two or three lines. Longer text pushes more useful content down the page.

faqs.q: Can I use the same objective for every application?
faqs.a: Reuse the structure, but change the role and skills to suit each posting.

faqs.q: What if I am changing fields?
faqs.a: Name the new field and the relevant skills or coursework you bring, for example: 'Mechanical engineering graduate with Python and data analysis training, seeking an analyst role.'

title: Common ATS Resume Mistakes and How to Fix Each One
description: Seven common resume mistakes that cause parsing or readability problems, with before-and-after examples and fixes for Indian job seekers.
h1: Common ATS resume mistakes and how to correct them

sections.title: Mistake 1: Contact details in the header, footer or a text box
sections.content: Some parsers do not read header and footer areas or text boxes, and Greenhouse lists these among the layouts that can cause a failed parse. The result can be a candidate record with no phone or email. Fix: place your name and contact line as normal text at the top of the page body.

sections.title: Mistake 2: Two columns, tables, icons and skill bars
sections.content: These look neat but can scramble reading order. A sidebar's skills might appear in the middle of your education section, and an icon carries no text at all. Fix: use one column and plain labels such as 'Phone:' and 'Email:' or a simple line with separators.

sections.title: Mistake 3: Image-only files and oversized documents
sections.content: A scan or screenshot saved as a PDF contains a picture of text, not text. Greenhouse documents that image uploads and files over 2.5 MB can fail to parse. Fix: export a text-based PDF or DOCX from your source document and test that you can select the text. Compress or remove heavy images.

sections.title: Mistake 4: Creative or unclear section headings
sections.content: 'My Journey', 'What I Do' and 'Things I Have Built' make people and software hunt for the sections they expect. Fix: use Education, Skills, Projects, Experience or Internships, and Certifications. You can still write a distinctive project description underneath.

sections.title: Mistake 5: Keyword stuffing, hidden text and unsupported skills
sections.content: Listing thirty tools, repeating a term in every line, or hiding extra keywords in white text makes the resume look inflated and can be exposed when the text is extracted. Fix: list the skills you can discuss and show the important ones inside projects or internship bullets.

sections.title: Mistake 6: Vague bullets with no evidence
sections.content: Before: 'Responsible for working on a team project.' After: 'Built the login and order modules of a canteen ordering app in React and Node.js with a four-person team.' The second line tells the reader what you did and which tools you used, which also gives relevant keywords a context.

sections.title: Mistake 7: Inconsistent dates, abbreviations and names
sections.content: Mixed date styles, 'Jan 24', '2024' and '01/24' in one resume, make it harder to read durations. Using only short forms for your institute or employer can also weaken recognition. Fix: use one date format and write full names of your institute and employers at least once.

faqs.q: Will a single mistake cause automatic rejection?
faqs.a: Usually not on its own. The more realistic risks are that your details are read incorrectly, your profile is harder to find in search, or a person finds the resume confusing. Some employers do add automatic rules tied to screening answers.

faqs.q: Are Canva resumes a problem?
faqs.a: Not necessarily, but many templates use columns, icons and text laid over images. Export, select the text, and check the plain-text result. If it merges or scrambles, switch to a simpler layout.

faqs.q: Is a two-page resume a mistake?
faqs.a: No. For a fresher, one page is a sensible aim, but a second page is fine when it holds relevant, non-repetitive content, as it might for a candidate with several years of experience.

faqs.q: Can I fix a mistake after I have applied?
faqs.a: Usually you cannot edit a submitted application, though some portals let you update your profile. Fix the file and use the corrected version for the next application, or contact the recruiter if a serious error needs correcting.

title: CV Format for AI Screening: What to Know Before You Apply
description: What 'AI screening' can mean for a CV, what is unknown, and how to format a CV that is clear to software and to the people who review it.
h1: CV format for AI screening: what helps and what does not

sections.title: What 'AI screening' can mean
sections.content: The phrase covers a wide range. Some tools only parse and search for keywords. Others try to understand related terms, summarise a candidate or suggest a ranking against a job. Online assessments and video interviews are separate again. Employers rarely say which they use, so any claim about 'what the AI wants' deserves caution.

sections.title: CV and resume: the terminology question in India
sections.content: In India the two words are often used for the same document. A one- or two-page document for a job application is usually called either one. A longer CV with publications, research and teaching may be expected for academic or research posts. For screening purposes, what matters is the structure and clarity of the document, not the label.

sections.title: Write for meaning, not only for keywords
sections.content: Some tools match related terms rather than exact words, but you cannot rely on that. The safest approach is to write complete, specific lines that make sense to a person and contain the right terms. 'Built a REST API in Flask for a library system, using PostgreSQL for storage' tells a reader and a tool more than 'Flask, PostgreSQL, API' alone.

sections.title: A structure that suits both machines and reviewers
sections.content: Use standard headings, one column, reverse-chronological order within sections and one idea per bullet. Start with the information that best matches the job. Spell out acronyms once. Keep sentences short enough that an automatic summary of your CV would not need to guess what you meant.

sections.title: What does not help
sections.content: Hidden text, such as white-coloured keywords or invisible instructions aimed at an AI tool, is a poor idea. It misrepresents the document, can show up when text is extracted, and may lead a reviewer to distrust everything else on the page. Copying the job description or inflating skills has similar risks.

sections.title: Keep a person in the loop and check accuracy
sections.content: If a tool summarises your CV, errors in the summary may come from unclear writing. Check that dates, employers, degrees and skills are unambiguous. Because you cannot see an employer's tools, aim for a CV that stays accurate and readable whether it is read by a person, parsed by software or summarised by a model.

faqs.q: Is AI screening free from bias?
faqs.a: No reliable claim can be made either way, because tools and settings differ. What you can do is present your information clearly and accurately, and avoid including details that are not needed for the role.

faqs.q: Should I use a different format for AI screening?
faqs.a: No separate format is needed. A clear, single-column CV with standard headings, accurate dates and evidence-based bullets suits both automated tools and human reviewers.

faqs.q: Should I add hidden keywords to improve my chances?
faqs.a: No. Hidden text can be revealed during text extraction and may be treated as an attempt to mislead. Put real keywords where they describe real work.

faqs.q: Will an AI tool read PDFs properly?
faqs.a: It depends on the tool and on how the PDF was made. A text-based PDF is generally easier to read than a scanned image, so check that you can select text before uploading.

title: Fresher Resume Format: How to Build One From Scratch

sections.title: Gather your raw material first
sections.content: Before you open a template, list everything you have done in the last three or four years: projects, assignments you are proud of, internships, workshops, competitions, club roles, volunteering, part-time work, courses and certifications. Write one line on what you did for each. Most freshers discover they have more material than they thought, and the work is then selecting, not inventing.

sections.title: Turn activities into resume lines
sections.content:
A club role becomes: 'Coordinated registration for a 300-participant technical fest; managed a four-member volunteer team.' A class assignment becomes: 'Analysed a 2,000-row survey dataset in Excel and summarised results in a presentation.' If you cannot state a number honestly, describe the task and tools instead.

sections.title: Pick the sections your material supports
sections.content: Use sections that have content. A fresher with two projects and a course may need only Education, Skills, Projects and Certifications. A fresher with an internship adds Experience. Do not add an empty 'Achievements' section just because templates have one.

sections.title: Order by what the job needs
sections.content: Read the job posting, then put your most relevant evidence first. If the role needs programming, lead with projects. If it needs customer handling, lead with a related internship or campus role. Keep education above the fold in any case because it is your core credential.

sections.title: What to leave out
sections.content: Leave out unrelated hobbies, a long objective, repeated skills, vague phrases such as 'hard-working' and a declaration paragraph. Leave out any skill you could not answer a basic question about, and any date or score you are not sure of.

sections.title: Review it like a recruiter
sections.content: Read the first third of the page and ask: what degree, what skills, what evidence? Then check spelling, date format, link accuracy and file type. Ask a senior or a placement officer to read it for five minutes and tell you what role it suggests.

faqs.q: What if I have no projects or internships?
faqs.a: Use coursework, lab work, assignments, competitions and campus activities, with a plain description of what you did. Consider starting a small project and describing it honestly.

faqs.q: Can I include school-level achievements?
faqs.a: Only if they are recent or directly relevant. For most roles, college-level work carries more weight.

faqs.q: Should I make the resume on Word, Canva or a builder?
faqs.a: Any tool works if the exported file has selectable text and a clean reading order. Check by pasting the text into a plain-text editor.

faqs.q: How long does a first resume take?
faqs.a: Gathering material takes longer than formatting. Once you have your list, shaping it into a one-page resume is quick, and later versions need only small edits.

title: How to Make Your Resume ATS-Friendly: 7 Steps for 2026
description: Follow seven practical steps to turn an existing resume into a clean, parseable one: rebuild, rename sections, export and test.
h1: How to make your resume ATS-friendly: a step-by-step process
keywords: how to make resume ats friendly
