sections.title: Step 1: Start with the job posting
sections.content: Open the vacancy you are applying to and note the job title, required skills, tools and qualifications. Your resume will be read against that posting, so decide which two or three of your experiences answer it best before you touch any formatting.

sections.title: Step 2: Rebuild in a clean, single-column document
sections.content:
If your current resume is a designed PDF, do not try to patch it. Copy the text into a fresh word-processor file or resume builder and lay it out as one column. Keep your original design file as a source copy, since you may use it for non-portal situations.

Remove tables, text boxes, icons, skill bars and images. If the file contains a photo, remove it unless the employer asks for one.

sections.title: Step 3: Use conventional section headings
sections.content: Rename creative headings to the ones people and software expect: Summary, Education, Skills, Projects, Experience or Internships, and Certifications. 'My Journey' or 'What I Bring' may be charming, but a recruiter searching for 'Experience' has to guess where yours is.

sections.title: Step 4: Rewrite bullets to show proof
sections.content:
For each project or internship, say what you built, with what, and what came of it. Weak: 'Worked on a website.' Better: 'Built a placement-cell portal in Django with student login and resume upload; tested with 40 users in the department.' Use numbers only if you can explain where they came from.

This step also puts relevant tools and terms in context, which is more convincing than a bare list.

sections.title: Step 5: Export the right file
sections.content: Follow the file type the employer asks for. If both are allowed, a text-based PDF or a DOCX is usually reasonable. Name the file clearly, such as 'Aarav_Sharma_Resume.pdf', and keep it small. Greenhouse says it cannot parse resumes larger than 2.5 MB, and other systems have limits of their own, so avoid heavy images and embedded graphics.

sections.title: Step 6: Run the plain-text test and read it as a recruiter
sections.content: Select all the text in the exported file and paste it into a plain-text editor. Check that name and phone number are present, headings appear in order, and dates sit next to the right roles. Then read the first third of the page as a stranger would: can you tell who this person is, what they studied and what they can do?

sections.title: Step 7: Save a master copy and tailor from it
sections.content: Keep one complete master resume. For each application, copy it and adjust the summary, the order of skills and the top two or three bullets to fit the posting. Name the copies by company and role so you remember which version you sent.

faqs.q: Can I make my existing PDF ATS-friendly without rebuilding it?
faqs.a: Only if it is already a single-column, text-based file. Fixing a designed PDF is usually harder than moving the content into a clean document, because the layout elements are what cause trouble.

faqs.q: Do I need to redo the process for each application?
faqs.a: The first pass takes the longest. After that, you mostly adjust the summary, the order of skills and a few bullets for each role, rather than rebuilding the page.

faqs.q: Which is better in 2026, PDF or DOCX?
faqs.a: Neither wins everywhere. Follow the instruction on the application page. If there is no instruction, a text-based PDF preserves layout, and a DOCX is a fallback if a portal struggles with PDFs.

faqs.q: What should I do if a portal rejects my upload?
faqs.a: Check the file type and size first, then re-export from your source document rather than renaming the file extension. If it still fails, try the other accepted format or contact the recruiter listed on the posting.

title: Indian Resume Format: Conventions and What to Skip
description: Understand Indian resume conventions: how to write marks, personal details, languages and declarations, and which traditions you can safely drop.
h1: Indian resume format: conventions and what to leave out

sections.title: Where Indian conventions come from
sections.content: Many traditional Indian resumes carry a photo, date of birth, father's name, marital status, address and a closing declaration. Government forms and some institutions asked for these, and templates copied the habit. Many private employers do not need them. Check what the application asks for before including any.

sections.title: Writing marks and qualifications
sections.content: List qualifications in reverse order: highest first. Write the degree, branch, institute, university or board, years and score in the same form as your marksheet. Add the scale for CGPA. Include Class XII and X if the form or sector expects them, as in many entry-level and government-linked applications.

sections.title: Personal details: a decision guide
sections.content: Name, phone, email and city are always useful. Date of birth, nationality, marital status and father's name are often unnecessary on a resume; supply them on a form if requested. A photo is usually unnecessary in corporate applications unless the employer asks. If an application is for a government or institutional post, follow its notification.

sections.title: Languages known and hobbies
sections.content: Languages can help for roles that need them, such as customer support in a regional language. State your proficiency level honestly: 'Hindi (native), English (professional), Punjabi (conversational)'. Hobbies are optional; keep them only if they show a relevant quality, such as a coding club or public speaking.

sections.title: The declaration paragraph
sections.content: The line 'I hereby declare that the information is true' is traditional but adds little in most private applications. If you drop it, accuracy is still your responsibility. If a government or institutional form wants a declaration, include it there.

sections.title: Modernising without losing what matters
sections.content: Keep the facts Indian employers rely on, such as degree, scores and dates, and drop elements that take space without adding evidence. Make sure the file stays plain and readable. NextCV's resume format guides explain the general layout; this page covers the local conventions.

faqs.q: Should I still mention my father's name on a resume?
faqs.a: For most private-sector roles it is unnecessary. Provide it when a form or document requires it.

faqs.q: Is it necessary to add the date of birth?
faqs.a: Not on most corporate resumes. Where an application asks for it, enter it in the form.

faqs.q: Do government job resumes follow this guide?
faqs.a: Not usually. They tend to follow notification-specific forms and document rules, so follow those.

faqs.q: How do I show regional language skills?
faqs.a: List them with an honest proficiency level, ideally in a short 'Languages' line near the end.

title: Latest Resume Format 2026: What Has Changed
description: What recruiters and tools now expect from a resume in 2026: skills-first evidence, clean layouts, linked proof and careful AI use, without a fixed standard.
h1: Latest resume format: what has changed

sections.title: There is no official 2026 standard
sections.content: No authority sets a resume format. What changes are common practices, shaped by how employers collect and review applications. The sensible approach is to follow stable fundamentals and adjust to what a job posting asks for. Be wary of any article that promises 'the' new format.

sections.title: Evidence first, adjectives last
sections.content: Recruiters reading many applications respond to concrete evidence. Projects, results, tools and outcomes carry more weight than lists of traits. Put relevant evidence near the top and cut phrases that do not support it.

sections.title: Cleaner, text-based layouts
sections.content: Application systems and review tools read text. Single-column layouts, standard headings and text-based files continue to be the safest choice. Decorative templates with columns, icons and images may look appealing but are more likely to cause parsing problems.

sections.title: Links and proof
sections.content: A portfolio, GitHub profile, published article or certificate link can help when it is current and relevant. Write links as visible text, check that they open and remove any that lead to empty profiles.

sections.title: AI-assisted writing and screening
sections.content: Many candidates use AI tools to draft resumes, and employers may use software to sort or summarise applications, though practices vary and are rarely disclosed. Review any AI-drafted line against your real experience, remove invented specifics and keep your own voice. A resume you cannot explain in an interview does you no favours.

sections.title: What has not changed
sections.content: Accuracy, relevance, readable structure and honesty remain the base. Reverse-chronological order, consistent dates and tailored content still do most of the work. If you want the structure in detail, see the Indian resume format and ATS-friendly resume guides.

faqs.q: Do I need a new resume format every year?
faqs.a: No. Update the content when your experience changes and adjust the order and wording for each job, but the basic structure stays valid.

faqs.q: Should I use an AI tool to write my resume?
faqs.a: You may, but check every line for accuracy and remove anything you cannot explain. The final document should reflect what you actually did.

faqs.q: Are video or graphic resumes better?
faqs.a: Only for roles that ask for them, such as design or media. For most roles, a plain text-based document is the standard.

faqs.q: Is a skills-first layout recommended?
faqs.a: It can help if your skills are clearly relevant, but keep dates and context so the reader understands where the skills come from.

title: Non-IT Resume Format for Freshers: Examples by Field
description: A resume guide for non-IT freshers in India: what to highlight in commerce, arts, science and management, with sample lines and transferable skills.
h1: Non-IT resume format for freshers

sections.title: Evidence looks different outside IT
sections.content: Without code to show, non-IT freshers need other kinds of proof: internships, coursework with practical output, campus roles, volunteering, part-time jobs and tool skills. The aim is the same: show what you did and what it involved, in terms a recruiter in your target field can use.

sections.title: Commerce and accounting graduates
sections.content: Show Tally, Excel, GST basics or banking coursework through something you did. 'Prepared monthly ledgers for a small trader during a three-week internship using Tally.' Add certifications such as a course in taxation or accounting software if relevant. Lead with the internship if you have one.

sections.title: BBA, MBA and management freshers
sections.content: Describe projects with a business outcome, such as a market survey or a campaign plan. 'Surveyed 120 customers on café preferences; summarised results and proposed a loyalty offer.' Add leadership roles in clubs or events and the tools you used, such as Excel, PowerPoint or a CRM tool.

sections.title: Arts, science and other graduates
sections.content: Translate academic work into skills the role needs. A BA student who wrote research papers can show writing and analysis; a BSc student with lab work can show data recording and accuracy. Include relevant tools, language skills and any content or community work, with examples.

sections.title: Transferable skills, shown properly
sections.content: 'Good communication' is a claim; 'Presented a research paper to a panel of 30 attendees' is evidence. Pick two or three skills the role needs, such as communication, coordination or analysis, and give one concrete example for each.

sections.title: Layout and role-specific tips
sections.content: Use a single-column layout, standard headings and one page. For customer service or sales, put internships or campus roles first. For HR or operations, show organising and coordination. For content roles, add links to published pieces. Check the job posting's required tools and show those you can use.

faqs.q: Can a non-IT fresher apply to roles without experience?
faqs.a: Yes, for entry-level roles. Show internships, projects, tools and relevant coursework to support your application.

faqs.q: What tools should a commerce fresher list?
faqs.a: Those you have used, such as Tally, Excel, accounting packages or a CRM tool, with a short description of tasks.

faqs.q: Do I need a career objective?
faqs.a: A short, specific summary naming your degree and target role is optional. Avoid generic lines.

faqs.q: How do I show soft skills without sounding generic?
faqs.a: Give one example for each: a presentation you gave, a team you coordinated or an event you organised, with a concrete detail.

title: Resume Making Charges in India: Builder, Writer or DIY
description: Compare resume making charges in India across DIY, online builders, local services and professional writers, with questions to ask before you pay.
h1: Resume making charges in India: DIY, builder or writer

sections.title: Four ways to get a resume made
sections.content: You can write it yourself, use an online builder, ask a local typing or print service to format it, or hire a professional resume writer. They differ in cost, control and the quality of content. Charges also vary by city and provider, so ask for a written quote and compare final totals.

sections.title: DIY in a word processor
sections.content: The cost is your time. You control the content and the layout. The risks are inconsistent formatting and exports that look different on other devices. Use a plain, single-column layout and check the exported PDF.

sections.title: Online resume builders
sections.content: They provide templates, structure and sometimes writing suggestions. Check what the free part includes, what a download costs, whether the fee recurs and whether you can edit later. Review any AI-written lines against your real experience before using them.

sections.title: Local typing and print services
sections.content: A neighbourhood service can type and print quickly, usually from the details you hand over. Ask for the editable file as well as the printout, check spelling of names and scores and look at the layout. If the file is image-only, it will be harder to use online.

sections.title: Professional resume writers
sections.content: A writer may interview you, rewrite your content and format the result. This tends to cost more than a builder and suits candidates with complex histories or senior roles. Ask for samples, the number of revisions included and a clear scope. Be cautious about promises of guaranteed interviews or job offers; no writer can promise those.

sections.title: Questions to ask before paying
sections.content: What exactly is included? How many edits? What formats will I receive? Is payment one-time? Can I get the editable file? Who owns the content? A clear answer to each is a good sign. For NextCV's own pricing, read its public pricing page for the current model and amounts.

faqs.q: Do freshers need to pay for a resume writer?
faqs.a: Usually not. A fresher with projects or internships can write a good resume with a builder or a template, then ask a senior to review it.

faqs.q: Should I pay someone who promises a guaranteed job?
faqs.a: No. No service can guarantee interviews or placement. Look for providers who describe their scope and revisions clearly.

faqs.q: Can I get the editable file from a local service?
faqs.a: Ask for it before paying. Having a Word or Google Docs file lets you update the resume later.

faqs.q: Where can I check NextCV's price?
faqs.a: On NextCV's public pricing page, which shows the current amounts and terms.

title: Resume for MNC Company: Applying and Positioning
description: How to approach a multinational employer from India: choosing the route, tailoring your resume to the posting, using LinkedIn and following up properly.
h1: Resume for an MNC company: how to approach the application
keywords: how to apply to mnc in india

sections.title: Routes into a multinational employer
sections.content: People reach multinational companies through careers portals, job boards such as Naukri, campus drives, recruiters on LinkedIn and employee referrals. Each route handles the resume differently. A portal may parse it into fields; a recruiter may read the file directly; a referrer may forward it with a note. Prepare a resume that works for all of these by keeping it simple and accurate.

sections.title: Tailor to the posting, not to the brand
sections.content: An MNC's name does not tell you what the job needs; the posting does. Highlight the role title, the skills and the responsibilities, then match them to your real experience. Lines that reflect the posting's wording, where true, help a recruiter's search and quick scan.

sections.title: Align the resume with your online profile
sections.content: Recruiters often check LinkedIn. Make sure the role titles, dates, education and skills on your profile match the resume. Use a professional photo on LinkedIn if you like, though it need not appear on the resume. Add a short headline with your target role and skills.

sections.title: Handling referrals and recruiter messages
sections.content: If you ask for a referral, send a short message with the posting link, one paragraph on why you fit and the resume file. Make it easy for the referrer. When a recruiter contacts you, reply promptly with an updated resume and confirm details they ask for, such as notice period for experienced candidates.

sections.title: Experienced candidates: results and scope
sections.content: Lead each role with what you owned and the outcome. Use figures only when you can explain how they were measured. State the team size, tools and domain. Keep the resume to two pages if you have several years of relevant work, and avoid padding with early-career detail.

sections.title: Follow-up and tracking
sections.content: Keep a list of applications with date, role, version of the resume and posting link. If a portal gives a reference number, note it. Follow up politely after a reasonable gap if a recruiter gave a contact, and avoid sending several versions of the resume to the same person.

faqs.q: Do I need a different resume for each MNC?
faqs.a: Not a completely different one. Keep a master and adjust the summary, skills order and lead bullets to match each posting.

faqs.q: Does a referral replace the resume?
faqs.a: No. A referral can bring your application to a recruiter's attention, but they still review the resume and your fit.

faqs.q: Is LinkedIn more important than the resume?
faqs.a: They serve different purposes. LinkedIn helps recruiters find you; the resume is the document they assess for the application. Keep both consistent.

faqs.q: How should I describe a career gap?
faqs.a: State the real dates and add a short line on what you did, such as study or caregiving, if you are comfortable. Avoid hiding gaps by changing dates.

title: BCA Resume Format for Freshers in India: Projects and Skills
description: A BCA fresher resume guide: how to present a three-year degree, programming coursework, mini and final-year projects and entry-level IT role evidence.
h1: BCA resume format for freshers

sections.title: What a BCA resume has to show
sections.content: A Bachelor of Computer Applications is a three-year degree, so you often have less project time than a four-year engineering student. Your resume should make the most of your programming coursework, mini projects and final-year project, and show you can build and explain simple software.

sections.title: Education and coursework
sections.content: List your BCA with university, institute, years and score. Add a short line on relevant subjects such as programming in C or Java, DBMS, web technology and data structures, if they match the job. Keep it to one line; the projects will carry the detail.

sections.title: Projects typical of a BCA course
sections.content: Examples: 'Built a student attendance system in PHP and MySQL with login and report pages.' 'Developed a console-based library tracker in Java.' 'Created an e-commerce front end in HTML, CSS and JavaScript with a shopping cart.' Describe your part, the tools and any testing. These are illustrative; use your own.

sections.title: The final-year project
sections.content: Give it the most space. State the problem, the stack, what you built and what you learned. If you worked in a team, list your modules. If a demo or repository exists, write the link as text and make sure it opens.

sections.title: Skills, certificates and entry-level roles
sections.content: Group skills as languages, web technologies, databases and tools. For web, support or testing roles, mention what you have used. Certifications from courses on web development, Python or SQL are useful when you completed a project through them. Entry-level roles such as junior developer, web developer, support or testing executive are common targets, but check eligibility on each posting.

sections.title: BCA to MCA or jobs
sections.content: If you plan to study further, say so in your own plans, not in the resume. For job applications, check each posting's eligibility rules, since some accept BCA graduates and others ask for specific degrees. Describe your practical skills and projects so reviewers see the work behind the degree title.

faqs.q: Can BCA freshers apply for IT jobs?
faqs.a: Many entry-level roles accept BCA graduates, though eligibility varies by employer and posting. Check each posting.

faqs.q: What projects should a BCA fresher include?
faqs.a: Two or three, including the final-year project, each with your role and tools. Quality of description matters more than the number.

faqs.q: Should I list C, C++ and Java together?
faqs.a: List the ones you have used in assignments or projects. If you have only studied one briefly, leave it off or mention it as coursework.

faqs.q: Is a BCA certification course worth listing?
faqs.a: Yes if it relates to the role and you did a project during it. Give the course name, provider and year.

title: MCA Resume Format for Freshers: Advanced Projects
description: An MCA fresher resume guide: how to show a postgraduate degree, advanced projects, dissertation work and your path from undergraduate study.
h1: MCA resume format for freshers

sections.title: What sets an MCA resume apart
sections.content: An MCA is a postgraduate degree, so reviewers often expect more depth than from a fresh undergraduate: larger projects, stronger fundamentals and clearer specialisation. Your resume should show that depth, in both the projects and the way you describe them.

sections.title: Show the education path clearly
sections.content: List the MCA first, then your undergraduate degree. If your UG degree was in BCA, BSc or another stream, that context helps the reader see why you moved into MCA. Give years and scores for both. If you did a lateral entry or a bridge course, keep it brief.

sections.title: Advanced and dissertation projects
sections.content: Describe a larger project in some depth: problem, architecture, stack, your role and results. For example: 'Developed a student placement portal using Spring Boot and PostgreSQL; built the REST APIs and role-based access; deployed on a cloud VM.' Include a short note on testing or deployment if you did it.

sections.title: Specialisation and tools
sections.content: Show the area you lean toward, such as web development, data analysis, cloud or testing. List the languages, frameworks and tools you have used, with a project behind each important one. Include data structures and algorithms practice if you have solved problems on coding platforms, with a profile link.

sections.title: Internships, papers and extras
sections.content: Include internships with specific tasks. If you wrote a paper or presented at a conference, add it with the title and venue. Certifications should support your specialisation. Keep activities that show teamwork or leadership short.

sections.title: How MCA differs from BCA resumes
sections.content: A BCA resume should show building basics; an MCA resume should show a step beyond: design choices, deployment, testing or analysis. If your MCA projects look like your BCA ones, say what is new in the later work, such as a framework or database design you had not used before.

faqs.q: Should an MCA fresher put the degree before projects?
faqs.a: Usually education first, then skills and projects. If a project or internship is your strongest evidence for the role, place it first.

faqs.q: How many projects should an MCA resume include?
faqs.a: Two or three substantial ones, plus any internship, with enough detail to discuss each in an interview.

faqs.q: Do I need to list my BCA details too?
faqs.a: Yes, as part of the education section. It shows your path and fills the timeline.

faqs.q: Is research work useful?
faqs.a: If it is relevant to the role, yes. List the paper title, venue and your contribution.

title: Resume Format in India: Types, Length and Sections
description: Understand resume formats used in India: chronological versus other types, how long a resume should be and which sections suit different candidates.
h1: Resume format in India: types, length and sections
keywords: resume format in india for freshers and experienced

sections.title: What people mean by an Indian resume format
sections.content: There is no single official format. In practice, an Indian resume is a one- or two-page document with contact details, education, skills and experience, usually in reverse-chronological order. The details vary with seniority, sector and employer, and the instructions in a job posting override any general rule.

sections.title: The main format types
sections.content: Reverse-chronological resumes list the latest item first and are the most common. Functional resumes group content by skill and are rarely preferred. Combination resumes open with a skills summary and then list history. For most candidates, reverse-chronological with a short skills section is the dependable choice.

sections.title: How long should it be?
sections.content: Freshers usually fit on one page. Candidates with several years of relevant experience may use two. Beyond that, a longer document is generally for academic or research positions, where a CV with publications is expected. Length should follow the amount of relevant content, not a number you want to reach.

sections.title: Sections by candidate type
sections.content: Freshers: education, skills, projects, internships, certifications. Experienced professionals: summary, experience, skills, education, certifications. Career changers: a summary that explains the transition, relevant skills and projects, then experience. Choose headings that a recruiter would expect, and skip sections that would be empty.

sections.title: Public-sector and private-sector differences
sections.content: Private-sector applications usually accept a concise resume. Government job forms often have their own fields and may require specific personal details, documents and attested copies. Follow the notification for those, rather than a private-sector resume template.

sections.title: Where to go next
sections.content: For Indian conventions such as marks formatting, personal details and the declaration, see the Indian resume format guide. For changes in what recruiters prefer now, see the guide to the latest resume format. For software-readable layout, use the ATS-friendly format guide.

faqs.q: Is there a government-approved resume format in India?
faqs.a: No general one exists for private jobs. Government recruitment follows each notification's own forms and requirements.

faqs.q: What font and size should I use?
faqs.a: A standard font such as Calibri, Arial or Cambria at 10 to 12 points. Use a slightly larger size for your name and headings.

faqs.q: Should I include references?
faqs.a: Usually not on the resume. Provide them if asked, and keep contacts ready with their permission.

faqs.q: Is a PDF or Word file better?
faqs.a: Follow the instruction on the application. If there is none, a text-based PDF preserves layout, and a Word file is a fallback.

title: CV or Resume in India: Which One Should You Send?

sections.title: Start with the situation, not the label
sections.content: Job posts often say 'send your CV' even when they want a regular resume. sections.title: Campus placement drives
sections.content: Your placement cell usually sends a required template or collects details through a form. Follow it. If you create your own, a one-page resume with education, skills, projects and internships is typical. Do not add a long list of publications unless the role relates to research.

sections.title: Job boards and company portals
sections.content: For roles on Naukri, LinkedIn or a company portal, upload a one- or two-page resume. Fill in the portal fields consistently with the document. Even if the portal says 'Upload your CV', a targeted resume is what most employers expect.

sections.title: Government and public-sector posts
sections.content: These typically follow the official notification's forms and document list, which may ask for specific personal details and attested copies. Follow the notification rather than a private-sector template.

sections.title: Higher studies, research and teaching
sections.content: For MS, MTech, PhD, fellowships, research internships and faculty posts, use a CV. Include education, research experience, publications or projects, presentations, skills, awards and referees if requested. Length can run beyond two pages when the content is relevant.

sections.title: Converting between them
sections.content: Keep a full CV as your master record and derive a one-page resume from it for each corporate application. Pick the most relevant items, trim dates and detail, and tailor the top section. This approach avoids rewriting everything each time.

faqs.q: Should I send a CV for a campus placement?
faqs.a: Send what the placement cell asks for. If it is open, a one-page resume is the usual choice.

faqs.q: Which should I upload on Naukri?
faqs.a: A resume of one or two pages. Keep your profile fields consistent with it.

faqs.q: What do I send for an overseas master's application?
faqs.a: Check the university's instructions. Many ask for an academic CV that includes research, projects and publications.

faqs.q: Can a fresher have a CV?

title: Tech Mahindra Resume Format: Pick the Right Version

sections.title: Why one resume may not fit every Tech Mahindra role
sections.content: A large employer posts for technical, testing, support and operations work, and each looks for different evidence. A single generic resume forces the reader to hunt for relevance. The better approach is a base resume plus small adjustments for each role family. The fresher-specific guide covers engineering graduates; this page covers how to choose the version.

sections.title: Reading a posting in three passes
sections.content: First, note the role name, required qualification and location. Second, underline the skills and tools mentioned, in order. Third, note any statements about shifts, communication or customer contact. Then ask which items you can support with real evidence. That list decides which sections go at the top and which lines you change.

sections.title: Technical role version
sections.content: Lead with skills and projects. Use specific tool names, such as Java, SQL or Selenium, and one-line descriptions of what you built or tested. Keep education brief if the posting is skills-driven. Include a link only if the repository or profile is clear and current.

sections.title: Support and operations version
sections.content: For customer-facing or process roles, lead with internships, volunteering, campus roles or part-time work that involved dealing with people or following procedures. Show tools such as Excel, ticketing systems or CRM software if you have used them. Add language skills and your comfort with the work pattern described in the posting, if you can truthfully say so.

sections.title: Experienced and returning candidates
sections.content: If you have a year or more of work, put experience above projects. Describe each role in terms of tasks and results, and keep dates consistent. If you have a break between jobs, show the real dates and add a short line on what you did, such as a course. Avoid vague explanations.

sections.title: Keeping versions organised
sections.content: Save a master resume and name each tailored copy by company and role, for example 'Name_TechM_Support.pdf'. Record the date you applied and the posting link. Before each submission, run the plain-text test and re-read the top third of the page. This avoids sending the wrong version or an outdated one.

faqs.q: Is there an official Tech Mahindra resume format?
faqs.a: NextCV cannot confirm that Tech Mahindra requires a specific format, so do not assume one. Use the layout the posting or your recruiter requests, and keep the structure simple.

faqs.q: Can I use the same resume for IT and support roles?
faqs.a: You can use the same base, but change the lead sections and the skills you emphasise. A technical and a support role look for different evidence.

faqs.q: What if the posting does not list skills?
faqs.a: Use the role title and responsibilities to infer relevant evidence. Show anything related to the main tasks, such as handling queries, writing code or testing.

faqs.q: How often should I update my versions?
faqs.a: Update the master whenever you finish a project, course or job, and re-check each tailored copy before sending it.

title: What Is an ATS-Friendly Resume? How the Software Reads It
description: See what happens to a resume after you click Apply: how an ATS stores, parses and searches it, where parsing fails, and what to fix.
h1: What is an ATS-friendly resume, and how does an ATS read it?
keywords: what is an applicant tracking system
how does ats read a resume
how ats works for job seekers

sections.title: What an applicant tracking system actually does
sections.content:
An applicant tracking system is software for managing a hiring process. It collects applications, stores candidate details, shows which stage each person has reached, and lets recruiters search and filter. Think of it as a database with a workflow on top, not as a robot that reads your resume and passes judgement.

A resume is 'ATS-friendly' when the software can pull the right information out of it without errors.

sections.title: What happens after you click Apply
sections.content:
First, the system stores your file and creates a candidate record. Second, it tries to parse the resume, reading the text and sorting it into fields such as name, email, education, employers and skills. Third, recruiters see the application in a list, often organised by job stage and date, and may search or filter it. Finally, a person decides who moves forward.

Employers can add screening questions at the application stage too. Those answers often matter as much as the resume, so fill them in carefully and truthfully.

sections.title: Parsing versus ranking: two different things
sections.content:
Parsing is extraction: turning a document into structured data. Ranking or matching is something else, where a product compares candidates against a job and orders or scores them. Not every system does the second part, and those that do vary in how visibly they use it.

Public claims that 'the ATS gives you 78%' or 'the ATS rejects 75% of resumes' rarely trace back to a reliable source. Treat any statement about one platform as true of that platform only, and be wary of confident numbers.

sections.title: Where parsing goes wrong
sections.content:
Greenhouse's support documentation lists several causes of an unsuccessful parse, including a file larger than 2.5 MB, a resume uploaded as an image rather than a document, and complex layouts with tables, headers, footers or text boxes, especially when your name and contact details sit inside them.

When parsing fails, a recruiter may have to type your details in by hand, or your profile may be harder to find in search. Other systems have their own limits, so keep the file small and simple rather than trusting a single published number.

sections.title: Naukri, career pages and campus forms
sections.content:
In India your resume may enter a system through a job board, a company's careers page, a campus drive form or an email to a recruiter. Naukri RMS, a recruitment platform from Info Edge, lists resume parsing and resume search among its features, and large employers often run their own portals.

For fresher drives, forms you fill in by hand frequently matter as much as the attached file. Keep your CGPA, degree names, dates and skills identical on the form and on the resume.

sections.title: Seeing your resume the way the software does
sections.content:
Paste your resume text into a plain-text editor. In a two-column resume with a sidebar, you might get something like 'Education B.Tech Computer Science Skills Python Java SQL 2021-2025 Projects', where the skills list has been dropped into the middle of your education details.

If you see that, the layout is the problem, not your content. Rebuilding the page as a single column fixes most of it. The format guide for India shows a section order that holds up well.

faqs.q: Is the ATS the thing that rejects resumes?
faqs.a: Usually not by itself. Many systems mainly store, organise and search applications, and recruiters make the decisions. Some employers do set up automatic rules, often tied to answers to screening questions, so read those questions carefully.

faqs.q: Do I need to know which ATS a company uses?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. If a job link takes you to a named platform, its help pages may describe supported file types and size limits. Otherwise a simple, text-based resume is the safest general approach.

faqs.q: Will the system read links to my GitHub or portfolio?
faqs.a: A hyperlink can be lost when a file is converted, so also write the address as visible text, for example github.com/yourname. That way both the software and a printed copy show where to find it.

faqs.q: What if the portal asks me to retype everything after I upload?
faqs.a: Auto-filled fields can contain errors, and some portals ask for manual entry anyway. Check every field against your resume, correct names, dates and scores, and keep one master copy so your answers stay consistent.
